speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked the Minister for Transport in respect of oBike's exit from the Singapore market, whether the Ministry will ensure that oBike will refund all unconsumed subscription fees to its subscribers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what is the notice period required by any shared bicycle operator to give to the LTA when it wants to cease operations; (b) what is the redress for users who have paid deposits for their services; and (c) what assistance can LTA give to these depositors.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: asked the Minister for Transport what statutory measures are in place to prevent private companies offering shared bikes or PMDs from defaulting on their public and customer commitments, such as service provision and deposits before the company goes into liquidation.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether there are safeguards in place for consumers to obtain refunds on their oBike deposits; (b) what recourse do consumers have should there be no refunds; and (c) how can the interests of consumers be protected when bike-sharing firms exit the market.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: First, oBike has attributed its decision to Government over-regulation.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Dockless bicycle-sharing services offer Singaporeans a convenient travel option.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We had deliberately adopted a light touch regulatory approach at the start, so as not to kill off this new innovative business model prematurely.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Now that we have actual experience of both the benefits, and the significant social disamenities caused by indiscriminate bicycle parking, we have decided to tighten regulations.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The licensing regime will reduce indiscriminate parking by requiring operators to internalise the costs of the social disamenities caused by their businesses, failing which, they should not be operating at all.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are mindful to minimise compliance costs for operators, as they could, in turn, be passed on to users.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: LTA finalised its regulations only after extensive consultation with the bicycle-sharing operators, including oBike.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We note that several operators have expressed their support for the new regulations.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Licence applications closed on 7 July 2018 and LTA has received seven applications.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: LTA will evaluate each application based on the strength of the proposal, especially the plans to minimise indiscriminate parking.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: LTA and the Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE) have met oBike to emphasise the importance of refunding user deposits and removing their bicycles from public spaces.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If LTA has to step in to remove its bicycles, we will impose fees on oBike for doing so.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: LTA and CASE will continue to engage oBike on its responsibilities.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Concurrently, as the company is in liquidation, CASE has advised that affected consumers should file their Proofs of Debt against oBike with the appointed liquidator, FTI Consulting.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Those who are unsure about how to file a Proof of Debt may contact CASE or the appointed liquidator for assistance.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Following oBike's exit, MoBike announced on 29 June 2018 that it would be waiving deposits for its Singapore users.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If the operators eventually do require user deposits when the licensing regime is implemented from October this year, LTA will study the need for bicycle-sharing operators to place a security deposit or performance bond.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Going forward, LTA will monitor and strengthen the licensing regime as necessary, as well as work with relevant organisations, such as the Personal Data Protection Commission, CASE, the National Parks Board and the Town Councils on public education and outreach, so as to strike the right balance between the viability of the industry and the interests of users and the general public.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Just a few supplementary questions for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: First, I thank the Senior Minister of State for sharing that the subscribers to oBike will have some recourses that the Ministry will look at together with CASE.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I wonder, given that the large number of subscribers that are affected, I understand close to a million, whether something could be done proactively to make it easier for each of these subscribers to get their subscription fees reimbursed, given the huge numbers involved.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: My second supplementary question is, I understand the light touch that the Ministry and, for that matter, the Government has adopted, to allow all these new innovations to take place.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But I guess a learning point from this episode is that we may need to recalibrate this light touch in the quest to bring these conveniences to consumers.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We have seen the bad side of this happening.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And this comment goes beyond the Ministry of Transport (MOT), rather the whole of Government, for any new innovations that are being introduced.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We need to just be aware that, sometimes, the light touch may be too light.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The first, whether it can be easier to get refunds, it is ultimately oBike's responsibility to refund the user deposits and I think we should not minimise that it is something for them to settle, something for them to seek out means and ways to serve their consumers and serve their customers as best they can.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As far as the light touch is concerned, I do agree with the Member.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I pointed out, it has not actually been that long since these business models appeared; it is just over a year.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: From a business point of view, there does need to be some runway for the business model to evolve, for the finances to be settled down, so we have to get the balance correct.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Where there are issues which are critical or dealing with personal safety, yes, we should be far more aggressive.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Where it is about social disamenities and behavioral change, perhaps we also need to learn the lessons so that, as a regulator, as well as potential future operators, we can find a way to best serve future customers and consumers of such a service.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Because, ultimately, these types of bicycle-sharing services are good for us because it will allow Singaporeans to make use of bicycles to close that last-mile gap in personal transport.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is also good for health; it is a possible leisure activity.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we do not want to remove these services in particular, and I think the general point that the Member is making is about how we need to have the right calibration between a light touch approach as well as leaving room for innovation and dealing with the social disamenities is absolutely correct.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: That is exactly what we are doing now.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Certainly, oBike, like all private companies, will need to comply with the Personal Data Protection Act.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, when they have no longer any use for the data that they have collected on their customers or their subscribers, and once they have settled all the issues with refunds and so on and so forth, there should be a full expectation that they remove all that data.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If these funds are with oBike, then I suppose the consumers will get back their funds.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: But many consumers have expressed concern that after liquidation, they will not be able to receive their refunds.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In the event that the consumers are unable to receive refunds from oBike, would LTA consider making a Police report against the directors of oBike to ensure a proper accounting of the funds that should be with the company but are no longer available for refund to the consumers?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But I think this issue falls under the Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act which is overseen by the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI).

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But as to how that plays out and what actions are taken and so forth, I think I would have to ask the Member to file the question for MTI as to how this might be managed in a way to serve the needs of Singaporeans as well as the businesses.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will stretch a little for one more question.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: One of the things that oBike did was to force its members to subscribe to its Super VIP (SVIP) using their deposit.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Will these customers be able to get a refund for these as well, because the decision to subscribe to the SVIP membership was done unilaterally without the customers' consent?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I do not know if it would be for me to comment about whether the service agreement between the users and oBike was appropriate.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
